calls.head: Top line on top line: Coronato vs. Eberle
calls.body: At home, the Flames keep sending Coronato’s line (Farabee, Backlund and Coronato) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Ryan Huska has been choosing strength on strength. Tonight the Kraken’s first line is McMann, Beniers and Eberle.

calls.happened: Calgary’s L1 (Farabee, Backlund, Coronato) spent 61% of its 5-on-5 time against Seattle’s L1 (6:36 of 10:44). The call needed 52%, halfway from the 38% it would get with no line matching to its home habit of 67%.

calls.title: Huska got his matchup
calls.plain: Calgary sent Farabee, Backlund and Coronato out against the Kraken’s first line for 61% of their 5-on-5 time, far more than the 38% they’d get with no line matching.
calls.said: Ryan Huska would send Farabee, Backlund and Coronato out against the Kraken’s first line again

calls.head: There’s no curse: Wolf vs. The Kraken
calls.body: Wolf has been shaky against the Kraken since 2023-24, well below his usual. But three seasons of data say a goalie’s record against one team tells us nothing about the next meeting, so don’t be surprised if he looks like himself tonight.

CGY.head: We had Calgary as slight underdogs (43%), and they pulled it off.

SEA.head: We leaned Seattle’s way (57%), but Calgary had other ideas.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Four points for Coronato as the Flames beat the Kraken
paras: Adam Klapka and Curtis Douglas squared off early in the first. Morgan Frost got the scoring started for the Flames on the power play early in the period. Frédérick Gaudreau tied it 1-1 for Seattle midway through the period. The second period was a wild one. Aydar Suniev, Matvei Gridin and Joel Farabee scored three goals in just under five minutes early in the period to put the Flames up 4-1. Seattle pulled Philipp Grubauer after four goals and turned to Joey Daccord for the rest of the second. Mackie Samoskevich cut Calgary’s lead to 4-2 on the power play late in the second, and Matt Coronato stretched the lead to 5-2 just 39 seconds into the third. Ryan Strome made it 6-2 with less than two minutes left. Coronato finished with four points on a goal and three assists, and Farabee had a goal and two assists.

Don’t let the score fool you: the chances were a lot closer than that. Dustin Wolf made 21 saves for the Flames. The Flames improved to 6-7-0 and climbed to fifth in the Pacific, while the Kraken fell to 8-5-1, third in the Pacific.

items.text: Mikael Backlund passed Johnny Gaudreau for fifth on the Flames’ all-time scoring list, with 610 points.
Berkly Catton has a point in six straight games.
Chandler Stephenson extended his point streak against Calgary to seven games.
The Kraken still lead the season series 2-1.
